assets.name: Player ship (Salamander FC P1 ship; P2 palette swap)
assets.work_note: Player 1 = sfc.player.p1_ship: in every posture (horizontal and vertical, level/banked, both exhaust frames) the body sprites are P0 20/22/02 and the nose/engine/exhaust sprites P1 20/27/16, exactly the Vic Viper scheme (level frame: 66 % / 34 % of the pixels in P0/P1; Gradius II $80: 72 % / 28 %), so player 1 keeps its NES colours. Player 2 = sfc.player.p2_ship (attr+9 = palette bit 0 toggled): body P1 20/27/16, parts P0 20/22/02 (66 % / 34 % in P1/P0), the rule Gradius II uses for its own 2-player ship $B8 (72 % / 28 %): a distinct red/orange second-player ship built only from Gradius II ramps, kept as is. Exhaust: P1 palette 1, P2 palette 0, as in Gradius II. The attr+4/attr+5 frames (whole ship in one palette: respawn/hit blink) stay. Pixel work (optional, no palette change): the Salamander body is darker than the Vic Viper (P0 slot 3 02 = 39 % of the ship pixels vs 30 %, white 20 = 17 % vs 26 %); moving the upper-hull 02 pixels to 22/20 gives the Gradius II light-on-top balance. The vertical-stage postures have no Gradius II counterpart (Gradius II has no vertical stages) and keep the same palette split. Drawing: outline ok (59 % dark rim; Gradius II player_ship 61 %)
